_comment: Seed CVE dataset for ProjectWARGATE cyberintel vector store. Contains high-profile vulnerabilities relevant to military/critical-infrastructure cyber operations. Based on publicly available NVD data.

descriptions.value: A command injection as a result of arbitrary file creation vulnerability in the GlobalProtect feature of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software for specific PAN-OS versions and distinct feature configurations may enable an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the firewall. Fixes for PAN-OS 10.2, PAN-OS 11.0, and PAN-OS 11.1 are in development and are expected to be released by April 14, 2024. Cloud NGFW, Panorama appliances, and Prisma Access are not impacted. This issue is applicable only to PAN-OS 10.2, PAN-OS 11.0, and PAN-OS 11.1 firewalls configured with GlobalProtect gateway or GlobalProtect portal. This is being actively exploited in the wild by state-sponsored threat actors.

An authentication bypass vulnerability in the web component of Ivanti Connect Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Policy Secure (9.x, 22.x) allows a remote attacker to access certain restricted resources by bypassing control checks. This vulnerability has been exploited in the wild by Chinese state-sponsored APT groups including UTA0178/UNC5221 to gain initial access to government and defense networks.

A command injection vulnerability in web components of Ivanti Connect Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Policy Secure (9.x, 22.x) allows an authenticated administrator to send specially crafted requests and execute arbitrary commands on the appliance. When chained with CVE-2023-46805, this allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Actively exploited by Chinese APT groups to deploy WIREFIRE, LIGHTWIRE, and other custom malware families on government VPN appliances.

Sensitive information disclosure in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway when configured as a Gateway (VPN virtual server, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or AAA virtual server. Known as 'Citrix Bleed', this vulnerability allows attackers to extract valid session tokens from memory, enabling session hijacking without authentication. Exploited by LockBit ransomware affiliates and nation-state actors against critical infrastructure including aerospace, government, and defense organizations.

Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0 (excluding security releases 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1) JNDI features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled. Known as Log4Shell. This vulnerability has had massive impact across enterprise and government systems globally, with exploitation by APT groups including APT41 (China), Phosphorus/APT35 (Iran), and Lazarus Group (North Korea) targeting defense, energy, and government sectors.

Jenkins 2.441 and earlier, LTS 2.426.2 and earlier does not disable a feature of its CLI command parser that replaces an '@' character followed by a file path in an argument with the file's contents, allowing unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files on the Jenkins controller file system. This is particularly dangerous in CI/CD environments used by defense contractors and government agencies, as it can lead to extraction of credentials, SSH keys, and build secrets.

Atlassian has been made aware of an issue reported by a handful of customers where external attackers may have exploited a previously unknown vulnerability in publicly accessible Confluence Data Center and Server instances to create unauthorized Confluence administrator accounts and access Confluence instances. Atlassian Cloud sites are not affected. This is a critical severity authentication bypass vulnerability affecting on-premise Confluence instances. Exploited by Storm-0062 (Chinese nation-state threat actor) to target government and defense organizations.

ConnectWise ScreenConnect 23.9.7 and prior are affected by an Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability, which may allow an attacker direct access to confidential information or critical systems. Known as 'SlashAndGrab'. Widely exploited by ransomware groups and APT actors within hours of disclosure. ScreenConnect is commonly used by MSPs serving government and defense contractors, making this a supply chain risk vector for military networks.

A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability (CWE-122) in Fortinet FortiOS 7.2.4 and below, 7.0.11 and below, 6.4.12 and below, 6.2.x, and FortiProxy 7.2.3 and below, 7.0.9 and below, 2.0.12 and below, 1.2.x, 1.1.x SSL-VPN may allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code or commands via specifically crafted requests. Known as XORtigate. FortiGate firewalls are widely deployed in military and government networks for perimeter defense. Chinese APT group Volt Typhoon has been observed exploiting Fortinet vulnerabilities to maintain persistent access to US critical infrastructure.

A out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS versions 7.4.0 through 7.4.2, 7.2.0 through 7.2.6, 7.0.0 through 7.0.13, 6.4.0 through 6.4.14, 6.2.0 through 6.2.15, 6.0.x and FortiProxy 7.4.0 through 7.4.2, 7.2.0 through 7.2.8, 7.0.0 through 7.0.14, 2.0.x, 1.2.x allows attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests. Confirmed by CISA as actively exploited. FortiOS SSL VPN is a primary remote access solution for DoD contractor networks.

Cisco is providing an update for the ongoing investigation into observed exploitation of the web UI feature in Cisco IOS XE Software. A privilege escalation vulnerability in the web UI feature of Cisco IOS XE Software when exposed to the internet or untrusted networks allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to create an account on an affected device with privilege level 15 access (full admin). This has been used to compromise tens of thousands of network devices globally, including those in government and military networks. The attacker can then use that account to gain control of the affected system.

A command injection vulnerability in the web UI feature of Cisco IOS XE Software, chained with CVE-2023-20198 for initial access. After creating a privileged account via CVE-2023-20198, attackers use this vulnerability to inject commands with root privileges. Used in massive exploitation campaign that compromised over 50,000 Cisco devices. Implant deployed allows persistent backdoor access to routers and switches forming backbone of enterprise and government networks.

An authentication bypass in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software enables an unauthenticated attacker with network access to the management web interface to gain PAN-OS administrator privileges to perform administrative actions, tamper with the configuration, or exploit other authenticated privilege escalation vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-9474. The risk of this issue is greatly reduced if you secure access to the management web interface by restricting access to only trusted internal IP addresses. Actively exploited in the wild.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software allows a PAN-OS administrator with access to the management web interface to perform actions on the firewall with root privileges. Chained with CVE-2024-0012 authentication bypass for unauthenticated root-level access. Palo Alto firewalls are deployed across DoD and intelligence community networks for next-gen firewall protection.

A missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in FortiManager fgfmd daemon allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or commands via specially crafted requests. Known as FortiJump. Reports indicate this vulnerability has been exploited in the wild since at least June 2024. FortiManager is used to centrally manage large Fortinet deployments common in government and defense networks. Compromise of FortiManager allows an attacker to manage all downstream FortiGate firewalls.

In Progress MOVEit Transfer before 2021.0.6 (13.0.6), 2021.1.4 (13.1.4), 2022.0.4 (14.0.4), 2022.1.5 (14.1.5), and 2023.0.1 (15.0.1), a SQL injection vulnerability has been found in the MOVEit Transfer web application that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to gain access to MOVEit Transfer's database. Exploited by Cl0p ransomware gang in massive campaign affecting hundreds of organizations globally including US federal agencies (DOE, OPM), defense contractors, and critical infrastructure operators. Used to exfiltrate sensitive data at scale.

A signal handler race condition was found in OpenSSH's server (sshd), where a client does not authenticate within LoginGraceTime seconds (120 by default, 600 in old OpenSSH versions), then sshd's SIGALRM handler is called asynchronously. However, this signal handler calls various functions that are not async-signal-safe, e.g., syslog(). Known as regreSSHion. Affects OpenSSH versions 8.5p1 through 9.7p1. OpenSSH is the primary remote access mechanism for virtually all Linux/Unix military systems. Theoretical remote code execution as root, though exploitation is complex.

In PHP versions 8.1.* before 8.1.29, 8.2.* before 8.2.20, 8.3.* before 8.3.8, when using Apache and PHP-CGI on Windows, if the system is set up to use certain code pages, Windows may use 'Best-Fit' behavior to replace characters in the command line given to Win32 API functions. PHP CGI module may misinterpret those characters as PHP options, enabling a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code. Actively exploited within 24 hours of disclosure. Affects PHP-based web applications on Windows servers including military web portals and administrative interfaces.

RARLAB WinRAR before 6.23 allows attackers to execute arbitrary code when a user attempts to view a benign file within a ZIP archive. The issue occurs because a ZIP archive may include a benign file (such as an ordinary .JPG file) and also a folder that has the same name as the benign file, and the contents of the folder (which may include executable content) are processed during an attempt to access only the benign file. Exploited by Russian (APT28/Fancy Bear, APT29/Cozy Bear), Chinese (APT40), and North Korean (Lazarus) state-sponsored threat actors in targeted phishing campaigns against government and defense targets.

Microsoft is investigating reports of a series of remote code execution vulnerabilities impacting Windows and Office products. Microsoft is aware of targeted attacks that attempt to exploit these vulnerabilities by using specially-crafted Microsoft Office documents. An attacker could create a specially crafted Microsoft Office document that enables them to perform remote code execution in the context of the victim. Exploited by Storm-0978 (RomCom), a Russian cybercriminal group, in targeted attacks against defense and government organizations attending the NATO Summit. Attack chain uses malicious Word documents.

Windows Common Log File System Driver Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows an attacker who has already gained initial access to elevate privileges to SYSTEM level. Exploited as a zero-day by Nokoyawa ransomware operators. The CLFS driver has been a recurring target for privilege escalation, with multiple zero-days found in 2022-2024. Critical for post-exploitation in targeted attacks against government systems.

Malicious code was discovered in the upstream tarballs of xz, starting with version 5.6.0. Through a series of complex obfuscations, the liblzma build process extracts a prebuilt object file from a disguised test file existing in the source code, which is then used to modify specific functions in the liblzma code. This results in a modified liblzma library that can be used by any software linked against this library, intercepting and modifying the data interaction with this library. Specifically crafted to target OpenSSH sshd through systemd, creating a backdoor that allows unauthorized remote access. This is one of the most sophisticated supply chain attacks ever discovered, attributed to a patient multi-year social engineering campaign. Had it not been caught, it would have compromised virtually all Linux SSH servers globally.

A vulnerability in the management and VPN web servers for Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to incomplete error checking when parsing an HTTP header. Exploited by state-sponsored threat actor UAT4356/Storm-1849 (ArcaneDoor campaign) targeting government networks. The campaign specifically targeted perimeter network devices across multiple vendors to establish persistent access to government networks.

A vulnerability in a legacy capability that allowed for the preloading of VPN clients and plug-ins and that has been available in Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an authenticated, local attacker to execute arbitrary code with root-level privileges. To exploit this vulnerability the attacker must have valid Administrator-level privileges on the affected device. Part of the ArcaneDoor campaign (UAT4356/Storm-1849) targeting government network perimeter devices. Allows persistence through device reboots via modified boot process.

Microsoft SharePoint Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability. An attacker who has gained access to spoofed JWT authentication tokens can use them to execute a network attack which bypasses authentication and allows the attacker to gain access to the privileges of an authenticated user. The attacker needs no privileges nor does the user need to perform any action. SharePoint Server is widely used across DoD and government agencies for collaboration and document management. When chained with CVE-2023-24955 (RCE), provides unauthenticated remote code execution.

Microsoft Exchange Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability. Known as ProxyNotShell. A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability that, when chained with CVE-2022-41082, allows authenticated remote code execution on Microsoft Exchange servers. Exchange servers are high-value targets in military and government environments due to the sensitive email communications they host. Chinese APT groups have historically targeted Exchange vulnerabilities (ProxyLogon, ProxyShell) for intelligence collection operations against defense and government organizations.

Scripting Engine Memory Corruption Vulnerability in Windows. A memory corruption vulnerability in the JScript9 scripting engine allows remote code execution when a user visits a specially crafted website using Edge in Internet Explorer Mode. Exploited as a zero-day by APT37 (ScarCruft/Reaper), a North Korean state-sponsored threat group, in targeted attacks against South Korean defense and intelligence targets. The attack specifically targets users who have IE Mode enabled, which is common in government and military environments due to legacy application requirements.

In JetBrains TeamCity before 2023.05.4 authentication bypass allowing to perform admin actions was possible. This allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution on TeamCity servers. Exploited by Russian SVR (APT29/Cozy Bear/Midnight Blizzard) in widespread campaign targeting software development infrastructure. TeamCity compromise enables supply chain attacks by injecting malicious code into software build pipelines used by defense contractors and government software suppliers.

Rust before 1.77.2 on Windows did not properly escape arguments when invoking batch files (with the bat and cmd extensions) via the Command API. An attacker able to control the arguments passed to a spawned process could inject arbitrary shell commands that would be executed by the batch file processor. Known as BatBadBut. This affects the Rust standard library and any Rust application that invokes batch files on Windows. Also affects other languages (Node.js, PHP, Haskell) with similar escaping issues. Relevant to defense software supply chain security.

In JetBrains TeamCity before 2023.11.4 authentication bypass allowing to perform admin actions was possible. This is a critical authentication bypass that allows unauthenticated attackers to take complete control of TeamCity servers. Rapidly weaponized and exploited in the wild within days of disclosure. Second major TeamCity auth bypass in 6 months, highlighting persistent risks to CI/CD supply chain security in defense contractor environments.

The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023. Known as HTTP/2 Rapid Reset. This is a protocol-level vulnerability affecting virtually all HTTP/2 server implementations (Apache, Nginx, IIS, etc.). Generated the largest DDoS attacks ever recorded (up to 398 million requests per second). Significant threat to military web services, C2 dashboards, and any HTTP/2-based infrastructure.

A server-side request forgery vulnerability in the SAML component of Ivanti Connect Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Policy Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Neurons for ZTA allows an attacker to access certain restricted resources without authentication. This is the third zero-day in Ivanti VPN products in January 2024, compounding the impact of CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887. CISA issued emergency directive ED-24-01 requiring federal agencies to disconnect Ivanti Connect Secure and Policy Secure products from networks. Demonstrates the cascading risk of perimeter VPN appliance compromise in government networks.

A code injection vulnerability in the User Portal and Webadmin of Sophos Firewall allows a remote attacker to achieve code execution. This was primarily targeted at organizations in South Asia. Sophos firewalls are used in government and military installations globally. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the firewall appliance. Part of a broader pattern of edge device exploitation by nation-state actors targeting network perimeter security devices.

Microsoft Outlook Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. Known as MonikerLink. A critical vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook allows remote code execution when a user opens a specially crafted email. The vulnerability bypasses Outlook's Protected View security feature by using a specific URL moniker format. No user interaction beyond reading an email is required (preview pane exploitation possible). Microsoft Outlook is the standard email client across DoD and government networks. Exploitation requires only sending a malicious email to the target.

Microsoft Outlook Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability. A critical vulnerability that allows NTLM credential theft via specially crafted emails. The vulnerability is triggered automatically when the email is received by the Outlook client - no user interaction (not even viewing) is required. Exploited by APT28 (Fancy Bear/Forest Blizzard), Russian GRU-linked threat actors, against European government and military organizations including NATO members. Used to harvest NTLM hashes for lateral movement in targeted networks. One of the most dangerous email-based attack vectors discovered.

Windows SmartScreen Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability. An attacker can craft a malicious Internet Shortcut (.url) file that bypasses Windows SmartScreen security checks. When a user clicks the shortcut, SmartScreen will not display a warning before executing the potentially malicious content. Exploited as a zero-day before patch availability. Later exploited by Phemedrone Stealer malware and other threat actors. SmartScreen bypass is a critical defense evasion technique that undermines endpoint protection on Windows systems used across military and government networks.

An unspecified SQL Injection vulnerability in Core server of Ivanti EPM 2022 SU5 and prior allows an unauthenticated attacker within the same network to execute arbitrary code. Ivanti Endpoint Manager (EPM) is used to manage endpoints across enterprise environments including government and defense installations. SQL injection leading to code execution on the EPM server allows an attacker to potentially push malicious configurations to all managed endpoints in the network. Added to CISA KEV as actively exploited.

Undisclosed requests may bypass configuration utility authentication, allowing an attacker with network access to the BIG-IP system through the management port and/or self IP addresses to execute arbitrary system commands. F5 BIG-IP is extensively used in DoD and government networks for load balancing, SSL offloading, and application delivery. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on BIG-IP appliances that serve as critical network infrastructure. Actively exploited in the wild.

Improper error message handling in Zyxel ZyWALL/USG series firmware versions 4.60 through 4.73, VPN series firmware versions 4.60 through 5.35, USG FLEX series firmware versions 4.60 through 5.35, and ATP series firmware versions 4.60 through 5.35, which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute some OS commands remotely by sending crafted packets to an affected device. Exploited by Mirai botnet variant to compromise enterprise-grade firewalls for DDoS attacks. Zyxel devices are used in small-to-medium defense contractor and government satellite offices. Compromise enables pivoting into internal networks.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's netfilter: nf_tables component can be exploited to achieve local privilege escalation. The nft_verdict_init() function allows positive values as drop error within the hook verdict, and hence the nf_hook_slow() function can cause a double-free vulnerability when NF_DROP is issued with a drop error which resembles NF_ACCEPT. This is a powerful Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerability with reliable public exploits available. Affects virtually all Linux distributions. Critical for military systems running Linux (servers, embedded systems, containers). Allows unprivileged local user to gain root access.

VMware ESXi contains an authentication bypass vulnerability. A malicious actor with sufficient Active Directory (AD) permissions can gain full access to an ESXi host that was previously configured to use AD for user management by re-creating the configured AD group ('ESXi Admins' by default) after it was deleted from AD. Exploited by multiple ransomware groups (Akira, Black Basta, Babuk, Lockbit) to encrypt VMware ESXi virtual machines. ESXi hypervisors host critical military and government workloads. Compromise enables mass encryption of all VMs on the host.

Microsoft Streaming Service Proxy Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges. The vulnerability exists in the Microsoft Streaming Service Proxy (MSKSSRV.SYS) kernel driver. Exploited as a zero-day in the wild. Local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in Windows kernel drivers are critical post-exploitation tools used by both nation-state actors and cybercriminal groups to escalate from initial user-level access to full system compromise on Windows endpoints.

In Cleo Harmony before 5.8.0.21, VLTrader before 5.8.0.21, and LexiCom before 5.8.0.21, there is an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability. Cleo file transfer products are used by enterprises and government agencies for managed file transfer (MFT). Exploited by Cl0p ransomware group in a campaign similar to the MOVEit exploitation. MFT products are high-value targets because they process sensitive data transfers between organizations, including defense supply chain communications.

ColdFusion versions 2023.6, 2021.12 and earlier are affected by an Improper Access Control vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary file system read. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass security measures and gain unauthorized access to sensitive server files. Exploitation does not require user interaction. Adobe ColdFusion remains in use in many legacy government web applications. File read vulnerabilities allow exfiltration of configuration files, credentials, and source code from web servers running ColdFusion.

A improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') in Fortinet FortiClientEMS version 7.2.0 through 7.2.2 and FortiClientEMS 7.0.1 through 7.0.10 allows attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via specially crafted packets. FortiClient EMS (Enterprise Management Server) manages FortiClient endpoint agents across networks. SQL injection allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Exploitation enables compromise of the endpoint management server, potentially allowing push of malicious configurations to all managed endpoints. Critical for organizations using Fortinet for endpoint management.

VMware vCenter Server contains a heap-overflow vulnerability in the implementation of the DCERPC protocol. A malicious actor with network access to vCenter Server may trigger this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted network packet potentially leading to remote code execution. vCenter Server is the centralized management platform for VMware virtualized environments deployed across DoD and government data centers. Unauthenticated RCE on vCenter gives an attacker control over the entire virtualized infrastructure. Added to CISA KEV as actively exploited in November 2024.

A deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.8 in Veeam Backup & Replication allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Veeam is widely used for backup and disaster recovery in enterprise and government environments. Exploitation allows attackers to compromise the backup infrastructure, which can be used to delete backups before deploying ransomware or to exfiltrate sensitive backed-up data. Exploited by Akira and Fog ransomware groups.
